selected_hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Phi Phi Islands Snorkeling & Island Hopping Tour
experiences.description: Embark on a full-day speedboat tour around the stunning Phi Phi archipelago, snorkeling in crystal-clear waters at Maya Bay, exploring Viking Cave, and swimming at Monkey Beach. Includes snorkeling gear, lunch, and hotel transfers from Krabi or Phuket.

experiences.name: Koh Lanta Beachfront Street Food Night Walk
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant beachfront night market on Koh Lanta, sampling iconic Thai street food including pad thai, mango sticky rice, grilled satay, fresh seafood, and coconut ice cream. Chat with local vendors and discover hidden food stalls along the shoreline promenade.
experiences.location: Ban Saladan Night Market, Koh Lanta, Krabi

experiences.name: Similan Islands Liveaboard Diving & Snorkeling
experiences.description: Join an overnight liveaboard trip to the world-renowned Similan Islands, one of Thailand's top dive destinations. Snorkel or dive among vibrant coral reefs, sea turtles, and reef sharks. Includes meals, equipment rental, and multiple dive or snorkel sessions across pristine beachfront sites.
experiences.location: Similan Islands National Park, Phang Nga Province

experiences.name: Koh Samui Beachfront Thai Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on Thai cooking class set steps from the beach in Chaweng. Learn to prepare classic dishes like tom yum soup, green curry, and mango sticky rice using fresh ingredients from a local morning market visit. Enjoy your creations beachside with ocean views.
experiences.location: Chaweng Beach, Koh Samui, Surat Thani

experiences.name: Railay Beach Rock Climbing & Sunset Kayaking
experiences.description: Spend a thrilling day at the car-free paradise of Railay Beach, accessible only by longtail boat. Try beginner-friendly rock climbing on the iconic limestone karsts with a certified guide, then kayak through sea caves and hidden lagoons as the sun sets over the Andaman Sea.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Thailand
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Phuket/Krabi Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange ferry or speedboat transfer to Phi Phi Islands (approximately 1.5–2 hours). Check in to your boutique stay, freshen up, and take a slow walk along Tonsai Bay to get your bearings and soak in the island atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Tonsai Village night market area. Explore the lively beachfront strip, browse local shops, and settle into island life.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the airport before or during your journey — grab a simple Thai rice dish or noodle soup from airport food stalls (approx. 80–120 THB).
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the ferry pier or on board — pack snacks or buy from pier vendors (approx. 50–100 THB).
meals.dinner: Tonsai Village street food stalls — try Pad Thai, mango sticky rice, or grilled skewers. Budget around 150–200 THB for a full meal.

day_by_day.notes: Book your ferry transfer in advance online to save time and money. Arrive at the departure pier at least 30 minutes early. October can bring occasional rain showers — pack a light rain jacket. Exchange some cash to Thai Baht before leaving the airport.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and head to Long Beach (Hat Yao) on Phi Phi Don for a peaceful morning swim. This is one of the best and least crowded beaches on the island in the early hours. Rent a longtail boat from Tonsai Pier (approx. 100–150 THB per person shared) or walk the jungle trail (20–25 minutes).
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a budget snorkeling day trip around Phi Phi Leh — visit Maya Bay (now open with visitor limits), Pileh Lagoon, and Viking Cave. Group tours from Tonsai Pier cost approximately 350–600 THB and include snorkel gear.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tonsai Village. Walk up to the Phi Phi Viewpoint (free, about 20-minute hike) to catch the golden hour sunset over both bays — one of the most iconic views in Thailand.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery or guesthouse café near Tonsai — banana pancakes or toast with coffee (approx. 80–120 THB).
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch box from a street vendor before the boat trip or eat at a beachside shack on Maya Bay island stop (approx. 100–150 THB).
meals.dinner: Papaya Restaurant or similar local eatery in Tonsai Village — green papaya salad, tom yum soup, and jasmine rice (approx. 150–200 THB).

day_by_day.notes: Maya Bay has daily visitor caps — confirm your tour operator includes an official permit. Bring reef-safe sunscreen and a reusable water bottle. The viewpoint hike is steep but worth every step.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a kayak from Tonsai Beach (approx. 150–200 THB per hour) and paddle around the dramatic limestone cliffs and hidden lagoons near Phi Phi Don. Head toward Monkey Beach for a close-up view of the resident macaques — observe from the water without feeding them.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Loh Dalum Bay on the northern side of the island. This crescent-shaped bay has calm, clear water and is perfect for swimming and relaxing. Rent a beach chair or simply lay on the sand for free.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Tonsai Village's street food scene more thoroughly. Look for the local vendors selling grilled corn, fresh coconut ice cream, and satay skewers. Enjoy a fire show performance on the beach — many bars host these nightly for free.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit smoothie bowl or rice porridge (jok) from a street cart near the pier (approx. 60–100 THB).
meals.lunch: Beachside food stall at Loh Dalum Bay — fried rice or noodle soup (approx. 100–130 THB).
meals.dinner: Street food dinner at Tonsai night market — mix and match dishes like spring rolls, som tum, and grilled fish (approx. 150–180 THB total).

day_by_day.notes: Be cautious with the monkeys at Monkey Beach — they can be aggressive. Keep bags closed and do not bring food near them. The fire shows typically start around 9 PM on the beach.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning ferry from Phi Phi Islands to Krabi Town (approximately 1.5 hours, 250–350 THB). Arrive in Krabi and check in to a budget guesthouse near Chao Fa Pier or the night market area. Drop your bags and head out to explore Krabi Town's local morning market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the iconic Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Suea) — a short songthaew ride from town (approx. 50 THB). Climb the 1,237 steps to the summit for a breathtaking panoramic view over Krabi's karst landscape and coastline. Allow 1.5–2 hours for the full climb and descent.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Krabi Town and explore the famous Krabi Night Market (Chao Fa Walking Street) which runs Friday to Sunday — check if it aligns. Otherwise, visit the riverside area near Chao Fa Pier for local food stalls and a relaxed evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the ferry or grab a quick bite at Tonsai Pier before departure — roti with banana and condensed milk (approx. 50–80 THB).
meals.lunch: Krabi Town local restaurant near the market — khao man gai (chicken rice) or pad see ew (approx. 60–100 THB).
meals.dinner: Krabi Night Market or riverside food stalls — fresh seafood, grilled meats, and Thai desserts (approx. 150–200 THB).

day_by_day.notes: The Tiger Cave Temple climb is physically demanding — wear comfortable shoes and bring plenty of water. Start the climb before 3 PM to avoid the hottest part of the day. October evenings in Krabi can be warm and humid.

day_by_day.morning: Join a budget four-island tour departing from Krabi Town or Ao Nang (approximately 500–700 THB including longtail boat, snorkeling gear, and lunch). Visit Koh Mor, Koh Chuak, Koh Tub, and the famous Chicken Island (Koh Kai). Walk the sandbar connecting islands at low tide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the island tour and visit Ao Nang Beach — Krabi's most popular beach resort area, a short songthaew ride from Krabi Town (approx. 50 THB). Stroll the beachfront promenade, browse souvenir stalls, and dip your feet in the Andaman Sea.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Ao Nang's street food scene along the main road. This area has excellent budget options and a buzzing atmosphere with travelers from around the world.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or local café in Krabi Town — toast, eggs, and Thai tea (approx. 80–120 THB).
meals.lunch: Included in the four-island tour package — typically simple Thai rice dishes served on a beach.
meals.dinner: Ao Nang street food strip — massaman curry, fried calamari, or a whole grilled fish (approx. 150–200 THB).

day_by_day.notes: Book the four-island tour the evening before from your guesthouse or a local tour office to get the best price. Bargain politely — group rates are often available. The sandbar walk between islands is only possible at low tide, so confirm timing with your guide.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longtail boat from Ao Nang Beach to Railay Beach (approx. 100 THB each way, boats run regularly). Railay is only accessible by boat and is surrounded by towering limestone cliffs. Explore Railay East and Railay West beaches, and hike through the jungle trail connecting them (10-minute walk).
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike up to the Railay Viewpoint for stunning panoramic views — the trail starts near the lagoon path and takes about 45 minutes round trip. Then visit the Princess Cave (Phra Nang Cave) on Phra Nang Beach, a sacred site adorned with colorful offerings. Swim at Phra Nang Beach, often ranked among the world's most beautiful.
day_by_day.evening: Return by longtail boat to Ao Nang before dark (last boats typically around 6–7 PM). Enjoy a relaxed evening back in Ao Nang or Krabi Town.

meals.breakfast: Local Thai breakfast spot in Ao Nang — congee with pork or fried egg with rice (approx. 60–100 THB).
meals.lunch: Beach restaurant on Railay West — choose budget-friendly options like fried rice or noodle dishes (approx. 150–200 THB — slightly pricier due to boat-access location).
meals.dinner: Return to Krabi Town for affordable local dining — try a curry house or noodle shop near the guesthouse (approx. 100–150 THB).

day_by_day.notes: Railay is one of the highlights of Krabi — do not miss it. Wear water shoes if available as the longtail boat landing can be rocky. Phra Nang Cave is a sacred site — be respectful. The lagoon hike beyond the viewpoint is very steep and muddy — only attempt with proper footwear.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge morning — sleep in, do laundry (most guesthouses offer cheap laundry service at 40–60 THB/kg), and plan the next leg of the trip. Visit Krabi Town's local fresh market (Talat Kao) for an authentic local experience and pick up tropical fruits like rambutan, mangosteen, and dragon fruit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a songthaew to Susan Hoi (Shell Cemetery) — a unique geological formation of 75-million-year-old fossilized shells forming flat slabs along the shore (free entry, approx. 50 THB for songthaew). Nearby, visit Khlong Haeng Beach for a quiet, uncrowded beach afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Chao Fa Pier area in Krabi Town for a sunset view over the mangroves and karst islands. Enjoy a leisurely evening walk along the riverside promenade.

meals.breakfast: Fresh tropical fruit from the local market plus a cup of Thai iced coffee from a street vendor (approx. 50–80 THB).
meals.lunch: Local restaurant near Talat Kao market — try khao soi (northern Thai curry noodles) or boat noodles (approx. 80–120 THB).
meals.dinner: Riverside restaurant in Krabi Town with views of the mangroves — fresh fish curry or stir-fried seafood (approx. 150–200 THB).

day_by_day.notes: This is a good day to rest your feet after several active days. Use the afternoon to book onward transport to Koh Lanta if needed. October is shoulder season — prices are often negotiable.

day_by_day.morning: Take a ferry or minivan transfer from Krabi to Koh Lanta (approximately 2–2.5 hours, 350–500 THB). Check in to a budget bungalow on Koh Lanta — Long Beach (Ao Phra-Ae) is a great base with affordable options. Settle in and take your first walk along the long, palm-fringed beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a scooter (approx. 200–300 THB/day) and explore Koh Lanta's coastline. Drive south along the main road, stopping at various beaches — Klong Dao Beach, Klong Khong Beach (known for its relaxed hippie vibe), and Klong Nin Beach. Each has its own character.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the charming Old Town (Ban Ko Lanta) on the eastern coast — a well-preserved stilted fishing village with colorful wooden shophouses, local cafés, and artisan shops. Watch the sunset from the old town pier.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure in Krabi or grab food at the ferry pier (approx. 60–100 THB).
meals.lunch: Beachside shack on Long Beach — simple Thai dishes like fried rice with egg or green curry (approx. 100–150 THB).
meals.dinner: Old Town restaurant or café — fresh seafood caught by local fishermen, grilled with herbs and lime (approx. 150–200 THB).

day_by_day.notes: Koh Lanta has a more relaxed, less commercialized vibe than Phi Phi or Krabi — perfect for those seeking authenticity. Scooter rental is the best way to explore. Always wear a helmet and check the bike before renting. October can bring some rain — plan flexible beach time.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Mu Ko Lanta National Park at the southern tip of the island (entry fee approx. 200 THB). Hike through jungle trails to a lighthouse with panoramic views, spot wildlife including monitor lizards and tropical birds, and discover the beautiful Tanod Cape Beach — one of the most pristine on the island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkel at the reefs around the national park or join a budget snorkeling longtail trip to nearby Koh Rok — known for some of the best coral reefs in the region (approx. 800–1,000 THB for a day trip including gear and lunch). Alternatively, relax on the secluded beaches near the park.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your bungalow and enjoy a sunset from Long Beach. Many beachfront bars offer happy hour deals (buy-one-get-one cocktails). Sit back and enjoy the Andaman Sea colors.

meals.breakfast: Bungalow breakfast or local coffee shop near Long Beach — eggs, toast, and fresh juice (approx. 80–120 THB).
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from a local vendor or included in the snorkeling trip.
meals.dinner: Beachfront restaurant on Long Beach — BBQ seafood platter or fish green curry with rice (approx. 150–200 THB).

day_by_day.notes: The national park is best visited in the morning before it gets hot. Bring insect repellent for the jungle trails. Koh Rok day trips are weather-dependent in October — confirm availability the day before.

day_by_day.morning: Take a ferry from Koh Lanta back toward the Krabi area and then onward to Koh Ngai (Koh Hai) — a small, peaceful island with crystal-clear water, excellent snorkeling, and minimal development (total journey approx. 2–3 hours, 400–600 THB). Check in to a budget beach bungalow.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon snorkeling directly off the beach — Koh Ngai has excellent house reef with colorful coral and tropical fish just meters from the shore. Rent snorkel gear from your guesthouse (approx. 100 THB) if not included. Explore the small island on foot — it takes about 30 minutes to walk the perimeter.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the ultimate island evening — a quiet beachfront dinner under the stars with virtually no crowds. Koh Ngai is one of the least-developed islands in the Trang archipelago and offers a truly peaceful escape.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure on Koh Lanta or at the pier (approx. 80–100 THB).
meals.lunch: Simple beach bungalow restaurant on Koh Ngai — fresh fish or fried rice (approx. 150–200 THB — slightly higher due to remote location).
meals.dinner: Beachfront bungalow restaurant — grilled whole fish, stir-fried vegetables, and steamed rice (approx. 200–250 THB).

day_by_day.notes: Koh Ngai is a hidden gem — one of the most beautiful small islands in Thailand. Food prices are slightly higher due to the remote location, but still very reasonable. Book bungalows in advance as capacity is limited. There is limited phone signal — enjoy the digital detox.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up at sunrise on Koh Ngai for a peaceful early morning swim in the turquoise water. Take a longtail boat to nearby Koh Mook (Koh Muk) — famous for the Emerald Cave (Tham Morakot). Swim through a 80-meter dark sea cave to emerge in a hidden lagoon open to the sky — one of Thailand's most magical natural wonders (longtail approx. 200–300 THB).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Koh Mook's Charlie Beach (Hat Farang) — a lovely stretch of sand with affordable bungalows and restaurants. Alternatively, take a longtail to Koh Kradan, known for its powder-white sand and exceptional snorkeling over coral gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Koh Ngai for your final night on this magical island. Enjoy a slow evening walk along the beach, star-gazing, and reflecting on the island-hopping adventure.

meals.breakfast: Bungalow breakfast on Koh Ngai — fresh fruit plate, toast, and Thai coffee (approx. 100–150 THB).
meals.lunch: Beach restaurant on Koh Mook — seafood noodles or fried rice (approx. 150–180 THB).
meals.dinner: Final dinner on Koh Ngai beachfront — splurge slightly on a fresh grilled barracuda or red snapper (approx. 250–300 THB).

day_by_day.notes: The Emerald Cave swim requires calm seas and is best done at low tide. Always go with a local guide or join a group — the cave is completely dark for most of the swim. A waterproof phone case or dry bag is essential. Confirm boat timings the night before.

day_by_day.morning: Take the morning ferry from Koh Ngai back to Krabi or to Trang Town (depending on your onward plans). If returning to Krabi, spend the morning revisiting favorite spots or doing any last-minute shopping at the night market for souvenirs — Thai silk scarves, elephant pants, local spices, and handmade crafts make great budget gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: If time allows, visit the Krabi Aquarium (approx. 100 THB entry) near Susan Hoi for a glimpse of local marine life. Alternatively, take a final relaxing afternoon at Ao Nang Beach or do a cooking class — several budget options available in Krabi for 800–1,200 THB including market tour and 3–4 dishes.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a farewell Thai dinner in Krabi Town. Revisit your favorite street food spots and try anything you haven't yet — tom kha gai (coconut soup), pad krapao (basil stir-fry), or mango with sticky rice and coconut cream.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the ferry or at the pier — roti with egg and condensed milk (approx. 50–80 THB).
meals.lunch: Krabi Town local restaurant — a final bowl of khao soi or boat noodles (approx. 80–120 THB).
meals.dinner: Farewell street food feast at Krabi night market — order several small dishes and share (approx. 200–250 THB for a generous spread).

day_by_day.notes: Use this day for any last-minute logistics — confirm your airport transfer for tomorrow, pack carefully, and keep essential documents accessible. Check luggage weight limits if flying. Consider sending heavier souvenirs home by post — Thailand Post is affordable and reliable.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Thailand — wake up early and take one last walk through Krabi Town or along the riverside to soak in the atmosphere. Visit a local temple such as Wat Kaew Korawaram (free entry) in the center of Krabi Town for a peaceful and reflective final experience in Thailand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange airport transfer to Krabi International Airport (KBV) or Phuket Airport (HKT) depending on your departure flight. Allow at least 2–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Do your duty-free shopping at the airport — Thai snacks, green tea, and local products make great last-minute gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Thailand with incredible memories of island-hopping, street food adventures, and stunning Andaman Sea sunsets. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final Thai breakfast — jok (rice porridge) with ginger and pork, or pad kra pao with fried egg from a local morning stall (approx. 60–100 THB).
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or food court — slightly pricier but convenient (approx. 150–250 THB).
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dining depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Keep some Thai Baht for last-minute transport and airport meals. Spend any remaining small change on snacks at the airport — Thai cashews, dried mango, and coconut chips are excellent travel snacks. Arrive at the airport at least 2.5 hours before international departure. Check visa requirements for your return journey.

trip_options.title: Classic Thailand Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing, clear customs and arrange a private taxi or shared shuttle to the pier. Take the ferry from Rassada Pier (Phuket) or Krabi Town Pier to Phi Phi Don Island. Check into your boutique hotel, freshen up, and take a relaxed stroll along Tonsai Bay waterfront to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Tonsai Village night scene. Browse the beachside bars and street stalls along the main walking street. Watch the sunset from the beach if timing allows.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack at the airport or on the ferry — convenience store items or a light airport café meal.
meals.lunch: Skip or grab a quick bite at the pier before boarding — try a simple Thai noodle soup or pad thai from a pier-side stall (~100–150 THB).
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local restaurant in Tonsai Village such as Papaya Restaurant or local Thai eateries serving green curry, tom yum soup, and jasmine rice (~200–350 THB per person).

day_by_day.notes: Ferry schedules from Phuket or Krabi to Phi Phi typically run until late afternoon. Book ferry tickets in advance. Keep arrival light — this is a travel day so don't over-schedule.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early and hike up to the Phi Phi Viewpoint (30–45 min uphill walk from Tonsai Village). The panoramic view over both bays is stunning in the morning light. Bring water and wear comfortable shoes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Long Beach on the southeastern side of Phi Phi Don for a relaxed afternoon of swimming and snorkeling in calm, clear waters. Rent snorkel gear from a beach shack (~150–200 THB). Alternatively, book a short longtail boat ride to nearby Monkey Beach to see wild macaques.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tonsai Village for sunset drinks at a beachfront bar. Enjoy fire shows that many bars host nightly on the beach.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel or a nearby café — fresh fruit, eggs, toast, and Thai iced coffee (~80–150 THB).
meals.lunch: Beach shack lunch at Long Beach — grilled fish, papaya salad, or a simple fried rice (~150–250 THB).
meals.dinner: Street food dinner along Tonsai Village walking street — try mango sticky rice, grilled satay skewers, pad see ew, and fresh coconut water (~200–300 THB total).

day_by_day.notes: October can bring occasional rain showers in the Andaman region. Carry a light rain poncho. Morning hikes are best done before 9 AM to avoid heat and crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Join a half-day snorkeling island hopping tour departing from Tonsai Pier. Most tours visit Maya Bay (The Beach), Pileh Lagoon, Shark Point, and Loh Samah Bay. Book through your hotel or a local tour operator (~800–1,200 THB per person including snorkel gear).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the tour by early afternoon. Relax on Loh Dalum Beach — the calmer bay on the north side of Phi Phi Don. Rent a beach chair and umbrella (~100 THB) and enjoy the turquoise water.
day_by_day.evening: Explore a different part of Tonsai Village. Visit local souvenir shops for handmade crafts, sarongs, and elephant pants. Enjoy a traditional Thai massage on the beach (~300–400 THB for 1 hour).

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl or açaí bowl from a trendy café in Tonsai Village (~150–200 THB).
meals.lunch: Packed lunch often included in snorkeling tours, or grab a quick bite at a beachside stall upon return (~150–200 THB).
meals.dinner: Sit-down dinner at a mid-range restaurant like Unni's Restaurant or a local seafood spot — try grilled prawns, red curry, and steamed jasmine rice (~300–450 THB per person).

day_by_day.notes: Maya Bay has limited visitor numbers and timed entry. Confirm tour operator compliance with national park regulations. Bring reef-safe sunscreen to protect coral reefs.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longtail boat to the quieter Phi Phi Leh island for early morning exploration before the crowds arrive. Visit the Viking Cave (ancient sea gypsy cave paintings) and enjoy the dramatic limestone cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Phi Phi Don and spend the afternoon at Laem Tong Beach on the northern tip of the island — accessible by longtail boat (~300–400 THB round trip). This secluded beach is far less crowded and ideal for swimming.
day_by_day.evening: Back at Tonsai Village, enjoy a cooking class experience if available through local operators (~800–1,200 THB). Learn to make 2–3 classic Thai dishes such as pad thai, green curry, and tom kha gai.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast before the early boat — try a hotel breakfast or a quick banana roti from a street vendor (~50–80 THB).
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Laem Tong Beach resort restaurant — fresh seafood platter or fried rice (~250–350 THB).
meals.dinner: Eat what you cook in the cooking class, or dine at a local restaurant afterward for a light meal (~200–300 THB).

day_by_day.notes: Longtail boats can be chartered directly at Tonsai Pier. Negotiate prices beforehand. Laem Tong Beach is home to the Moken sea gypsy community — be respectful of their culture and privacy.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Phi Phi Islands by morning ferry to Krabi Town (approximately 1.5–2 hours). Check into a mid-range guesthouse or boutique hotel in Krabi Town or Ao Nang area. Drop off luggage and head out to explore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the iconic Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Suea) — climb 1,237 steps to the summit for sweeping views of Krabi's karst landscape and rice paddies. Allow 1.5–2 hours for the full climb and descent.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Krabi Town's riverside walking street market (Thanon Khong Kha) for evening street food. The night market runs along the river and is a local favorite.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Phi Phi hotel before checkout — or a quick bite at the pier.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Krabi Town after arrival — try a local restaurant serving khao man gai (poached chicken rice) or boat noodles (~100–150 THB).
meals.dinner: Street food at Krabi Town Night Market — grilled seafood, som tum (papaya salad), sticky rice, and fresh tropical fruit (~200–300 THB for a full spread).

day_by_day.notes: The Tiger Cave Temple climb is strenuous and best done before 4 PM. Wear modest clothing as it is a working temple. Bring water. Ferry from Phi Phi to Krabi departs Tonsai Pier — book in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Join a full-day 4 Islands Tour departing from Ao Nang or Krabi Town pier. The tour typically visits Koh Mook (Emerald Cave), Koh Kradan, Koh Ngai, and Koh Chueak — pristine islands with incredible snorkeling (~900–1,400 THB per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the 4 Islands Tour — snorkeling at coral reefs, relaxing on white sand beaches, and swimming in emerald-green water. Lunch is usually included on the boat.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ao Nang by late afternoon. Enjoy sunset from Ao Nang Beach promenade. Explore the Ao Nang strip of restaurants and shops.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or a café near the pier before departure (~100–150 THB).
meals.lunch: Included in the tour — typically a simple Thai buffet on a larger boat or packed lunch on a longtail (~included in tour price).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ao Nang — try Last Fisherman Bar for seafood with a beach view, or a local Thai restaurant on the main strip (~300–500 THB per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book the 4 Islands Tour the day before through your hotel or a local agency. October weather can be unpredictable — check forecasts. Tours may be cancelled in rough seas.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longtail boat from Ao Nang to Railay Beach (15–20 minutes, ~100 THB each way) — accessible only by boat due to surrounding limestone cliffs. Explore Railay East and Railay West beaches in the morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike to Phra Nang Cave (Princess Cave) on the southern tip of the Railay peninsula — a sacred shrine with stunning beach views. Attempt the short but steep jungle trail to Railay Viewpoint for panoramic vistas. Try rock climbing at one of Railay's famous climbing schools (~1,000–1,500 THB for a half-day beginner session).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a beachside bar on Railay West — one of the most beautiful sunset spots in all of Thailand. Return to Ao Nang by longtail after dark.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel in Ao Nang before heading to the pier (~100–150 THB).
meals.lunch: Lunch at a restaurant on Railay Beach — fresh seafood, fried rice, or green curry (~200–300 THB).
meals.dinner: Back in Ao Nang — try a local Thai restaurant off the main tourist strip for more authentic and affordable food (~200–350 THB per person).

day_by_day.notes: Longtail boats to Railay run throughout the day from Ao Nang Beach. The last boats back are around 9–10 PM. Railay has no roads or vehicles — it's a peaceful, car-free zone.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Krabi to Koh Lanta by ferry or minivan-ferry combo (approximately 2–3 hours, ~350–500 THB). Check into a mid-range bungalow or boutique resort on the west coast. Relax and settle in.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Koh Lanta Old Town (Ban Sala Dan) — a charming stilted fishing village with colorful wooden shophouses, local cafés, and artisan shops along the pier. Learn about the island's Muslim fishing community culture.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from Long Beach (Hat Khlong Dao) — Koh Lanta's most popular beach. Enjoy the laid-back atmosphere with far fewer crowds than Phi Phi or Ao Nang.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Krabi/Ao Nang hotel or grab something at the pier before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Koh Lanta Old Town — try a local Muslim-style Thai restaurant serving massaman curry or fresh grilled fish (~150–250 THB).
meals.dinner: Beachside dinner at a restaurant on Long Beach — fresh seafood barbecue or Thai curry with a sea view (~300–450 THB per person).

day_by_day.notes: Koh Lanta has a significant Muslim population — dress modestly when visiting Old Town and be respectful of local customs. Renting a scooter (~200–300 THB/day) is the best way to explore the island.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter and explore Koh Lanta's west coast beaches from north to south — Khlong Dao Beach, Phra Ae Beach (Long Beach), and Khlong Khong Beach. Each has a distinct vibe from family-friendly to bohemian.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Mu Ko Lanta National Park at the southern tip of the island. Hike through the jungle to the lighthouse for panoramic views. Explore tide pools and mangrove walkways (~200 THB park entry fee).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Khlong Nin Beach for the evening — this stretch has a cluster of excellent restaurants and bars with a relaxed, artsy atmosphere. Enjoy live music at one of the beachside spots.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your resort or a café near Long Beach — fresh fruit platter, eggs, and Thai iced tea (~100–150 THB).
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at a beachside shack along Phra Ae Beach — pad thai, som tum, or a fresh fruit smoothie (~150–200 THB).
meals.dinner: Dinner at a restaurant on Khlong Nin Beach — try the locally loved Where Else? Bar or similar spots for wood-fired pizza or Thai fusion (~300–450 THB).

day_by_day.notes: The road to the national park is paved but can be steep in places. Take care on scooters after rain. The park closes at 6 PM. Fuel up your scooter in Ban Sala Dan before heading south.

day_by_day.morning: Join a morning snorkeling trip to the Koh Haa islands (5 islands) — one of the best dive and snorkel sites in the region with vibrant coral gardens and diverse marine life (~1,200–1,800 THB per person including equipment and lunch).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue snorkeling at Koh Rok — a protected national park island with crystal-clear water and stunning coral reefs. The twin islands of Koh Rok Nai and Koh Rok Nok offer excellent visibility.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Koh Lanta by late afternoon. Enjoy a relaxing Thai massage at a beachside spa (~350–500 THB for 1 hour). Spend a quiet evening at your resort.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your resort before the tour departure (~100–150 THB or included).
meals.lunch: Lunch included in the snorkeling tour — typically a Thai buffet on the boat.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local restaurant near your resort — try a simple massaman curry or stir-fried morning glory with rice (~200–300 THB).

day_by_day.notes: Koh Haa and Koh Rok tours are popular — book one day in advance. These are national park waters so reef-safe sunscreen is mandatory. Visibility is typically excellent in October.

day_by_day.morning: Travel back to Krabi or Phuket by ferry/minivan. If heading to Phuket, arrange a minivan-ferry transfer (~400–600 THB, approximately 3–4 hours). Check into a mid-range hotel in Patong, Kata, or Karon Beach area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Settle in and explore your Phuket beach area. Head to Kata Beach or Karon Beach for a swim — these are calmer and less crowded than Patong. Rent a sun lounger and enjoy the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Patong's famous Bangla Road night scene — a vibrant (and lively) entertainment street. Browse the night market stalls, try street food, and enjoy the energy of Phuket's nightlife hub.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Koh Lanta resort before checkout.
meals.lunch: Quick lunch during the transfer — grab food at a rest stop or pier-side stall (~100–150 THB).
meals.dinner: Street food dinner at Patong Night Market or local restaurants near Bangla Road — try grilled prawns, pad thai, and mango sticky rice (~200–350 THB).

day_by_day.notes: Bangla Road is very lively — be aware of your surroundings and belongings. If you prefer a quieter evening, Kata and Karon areas have excellent restaurants without the Patong chaos.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Phuket Old Town in the morning — a beautifully preserved Sino-Portuguese historic district with colorful shophouses, street art murals, and excellent cafés. Walk along Thalang Road and Soi Romanee (the most photogenic street).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Big Buddha — the 45-meter white marble Maravija Buddha statue on Nakkerd Hill. Stunning 360-degree views of Phuket island. Nearby Wat Chalong is Phuket's most important Buddhist temple and worth a visit (~30–45 minutes). Take a tuk-tuk or rent a scooter to get around (~200–300 THB for tuk-tuk round trip).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Promthep Cape for Phuket's most famous sunset viewpoint — arrive 30–45 minutes early to secure a good spot. End the evening with a farewell seafood dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast in Phuket Old Town — try a classic kaya toast with soft-boiled eggs and Thai coffee at a heritage café like China Inn or Kopitiam (~150–200 THB).
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant in Phuket Old Town — try Roti Talay (seafood roti) or a local curry shop (~150–250 THB).
meals.dinner: Farewell seafood dinner at a restaurant near Rawai Beach or Chalong Bay — fresh lobster, grilled fish, and prawns cooked to order (~400–600 THB per person for a special meal).

day_by_day.notes: Phuket Old Town is best explored on foot. Wear comfortable walking shoes. Dress modestly when visiting Wat Chalong (cover shoulders and knees). The Big Buddha is free to enter but donations are welcome.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Thailand — enjoy a leisurely breakfast and do any last-minute souvenir shopping. Visit a local market or pharmacy for Thai products to bring home (tiger balm, herbal products, Thai silk, etc.).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, either relax at your hotel pool, visit a nearby beach for a final swim, or head to the airport. Phuket International Airport is approximately 30–45 minutes from most beach areas (~300–500 THB by metered taxi or Grab app).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Phuket International Airport. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final Thai breakfast — try a hotel buffet or a local spot for jok (rice congee), fresh fruit, and Thai iced coffee (~100–200 THB).
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the hotel or at the airport — pad thai, fried rice, or a noodle soup (~150–250 THB).
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the airport at least 2.5–3 hours before international departure. Use the Grab app for reliable and fair-priced taxi service in Phuket. Ensure you have no prohibited items (fresh fruit, liquids over 100ml) in carry-on luggage.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Thailand Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Clear customs and collect luggage at Suvarnabhumi or Phuket Airport, then arrange a premium private transfer to the pier. Board a luxury speedboat charter to Phi Phi Islands (approximately 1.5–2 hours from Phuket). Check into your boutique stay, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome drink while taking in the stunning island views from your accommodation.
day_by_day.evening: Take a leisurely stroll along Tonsai Bay waterfront to orient yourself with the island. Watch the dramatic Phi Phi sunset from a beachside vantage point, then settle in for your first island dinner.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in transit
meals.lunch: Light refreshments at the airport lounge or grab a premium snack on the speedboat transfer
meals.dinner: Dinner at Unni's Restaurant on Phi Phi — a beloved island institution known for fresh seafood, authentic Thai curries, and a relaxed yet refined ambiance overlooking the bay

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange your private speedboat transfer before arrival to avoid delays. October is the shoulder season on Phi Phi — expect lush greenery, fewer crowds, and occasional short rain showers. Pack a light rain jacket in your carry-on.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a sunrise yoga session on the beach arranged through your boutique stay. Follow with a guided snorkeling excursion to the crystal-clear waters around Phi Phi Leh, including the world-famous Maya Bay (The Beach). Explore the stunning limestone karsts and vibrant coral gardens with a private guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Pileh Lagoon and Loh Samah Bay by private longtail boat — swim in the emerald-green enclosed lagoon and enjoy a gourmet picnic lunch prepared by your hotel on a secluded beach. Stop at Viking Cave to view ancient cave paintings and swiftlet nests.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a relaxing spa treatment — opt for a traditional Thai massage or a coconut oil body wrap at your boutique stay's wellness facilities. Enjoy cocktails at a cliffside bar for panoramic night views.

meals.breakfast: Tropical fruit platters, fresh-baked pastries, and Thai-style congee at your hotel's beachfront breakfast service
meals.lunch: Private gourmet picnic on the boat featuring chilled seafood, artisan sandwiches, fresh fruit, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Fine dining at Le Grand Bleu on Phi Phi — renowned for its Mediterranean-Thai fusion menu, fresh lobster, and premium wine list in an elegant open-air setting

day_by_day.notes: Maya Bay has restricted visitor hours to protect the ecosystem — confirm current access rules with your guide. Book the private boat charter the evening before to secure early morning departure.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on a premium island-hopping speedboat day trip departing from Phi Phi. First stop: Bamboo Island (Koh Mai Phai) — one of the most pristine white-sand beaches in the Andaman Sea. Swim, snorkel the surrounding reef, and enjoy the untouched natural beauty.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Mosquito Island (Koh Yung) for world-class snorkeling among sea turtles and tropical fish. Then cruise to the stunning sandbars near Koh Bida Nok for free diving and underwater photography. Your private guide will provide premium snorkeling gear and underwater cameras.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phi Phi by late afternoon. Head to the Phi Phi Viewpoint for a breathtaking panoramic sunset walk (approximately 20-minute hike). Reward yourself with sundowner cocktails at a rooftop bar overlooking the twin bays.

meals.breakfast: Full Thai breakfast at the hotel — jasmine rice soup, pad kra pao, fresh tropical juices, and strong Thai coffee
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood BBQ on Bamboo Island — grilled tiger prawns, whole fish, and papaya salad prepared by your boat crew
meals.dinner: Beachfront dinner at Ciao Bella Italian Restaurant, Phi Phi — indulge in wood-fired pizza, handmade pasta, and Italian wines with your feet nearly in the sand

day_by_day.notes: Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a rash guard, and a dry bag for electronics. The viewpoint hike can be slippery after rain — wear proper footwear.

day_by_day.morning: Arrange a private transfer by speedboat to Krabi Town (approximately 45 minutes). Explore the vibrant Krabi Walking Street Market in the morning for local handicrafts, fresh tropical fruit, and authentic street food tastings. Visit the iconic Chao Fah Pier and the quirky giant crab sculpture landmark.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hire a private longtail boat for a tour of the Four Islands (Koh Mor, Koh Tub, Koh Chicken, Koh Poda). Swim through a natural sea arch, walk across a sandbar that appears only at low tide, and snorkel in pristine waters. A knowledgeable local guide will narrate the cultural and ecological significance of each island.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Krabi Town for an immersive street food tour with a private culinary guide. Explore the night market along Maharaj Road, sampling pad see ew, fresh oyster omelets, mango sticky rice, and grilled satay from the best local vendors.

meals.breakfast: Artisan café breakfast at The Coffee Club Krabi — eggs Benedict, avocado toast, and specialty Thai iced coffee
meals.lunch: Freshly caught seafood lunch on Koh Poda Island — grilled fish, steamed clams, and coconut rice served on the beach
meals.dinner: Guided premium street food tour dinner in Krabi Night Market — curated tastings from 8–10 of the best stalls, paired with fresh coconut water and local craft beer

day_by_day.notes: The sandbar between Koh Tub and Koh Mor is only accessible at low tide — check tide schedules in advance and plan your Four Islands tour accordingly. Overnight stay in Krabi Town at a 5-star property recommended if not returning to Phi Phi.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to the Emerald Cave (Tham Morakot) on Koh Mook by private speedboat from Krabi. Swim through a narrow 80-meter dark tunnel to discover a hidden beach enclosed by towering limestone cliffs — one of Thailand's most magical natural secrets. Best experienced at low tide with minimal crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue island hopping to Koh Kradan — consistently ranked among Thailand's most beautiful islands. Enjoy snorkeling over a spectacular house reef teeming with reef sharks, rays, and colorful coral. Relax on the powdery white beach with a premium beach setup (sun loungers, umbrella, and chilled towel service) arranged through your tour operator.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your Phi Phi boutique stay by private speedboat. Enjoy a private beachside dinner set up by your hotel — candles, fresh flowers, and a custom menu prepared by the in-house chef.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel before departure — fresh fruit, yogurt parfait, and energy bars for the boat journey
meals.lunch: Gourmet beach picnic on Koh Kradan — chilled seafood platter, artisan cheeses, tropical fruits, and chilled rosé wine
meals.dinner: Private romantic beachside dinner at your boutique stay — 4-course Thai tasting menu featuring tom yum goong, massaman lamb, and mango sorbet

day_by_day.notes: Emerald Cave requires swimming ability and comfort in dark enclosed spaces. Life jackets are provided. This day involves significant boat travel — bring motion sickness remedies if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to a deep-dive snorkeling or beginner scuba diving experience around Phi Phi's best dive sites — Hin Phae, Bida Nok, and Bida Nai. These sites are home to leopard sharks, reef sharks, sea turtles, and spectacular coral walls. Book through a PADI-certified dive center for a premium guided experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for a leisurely afternoon by the pool or on your private beach. Indulge in a 90-minute couples spa treatment — choose from a traditional Thai herbal compress massage, hot stone therapy, or a signature coconut and lemongrass scrub.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Tonsai Village night scene. Browse local artisan shops and galleries, then join a Thai cooking class at a boutique culinary studio — learn to make green curry, pad thai, and mango sticky rice from scratch with a professional chef.

meals.breakfast: Poolside breakfast at the hotel — smoothie bowls, eggs your way, and fresh-pressed tropical juices
meals.lunch: Post-dive lunch at Papaya Restaurant, Phi Phi — hearty Thai comfort food including khao man gai, som tum, and fresh coconut
meals.dinner: Enjoy the dishes you prepared in your cooking class as your dinner, complemented by Thai craft beers and herbal teas

day_by_day.notes: If you are not a certified diver, most dive centers offer a half-day Discover Scuba Diving experience that requires no prior certification. Book the cooking class 24 hours in advance as group sizes are limited.

day_by_day.morning: Take a private speedboat transfer to Railay Beach in Krabi Province (approximately 30–45 minutes) — one of Thailand's most spectacular beaches, accessible only by boat due to towering limestone cliffs. Explore Railay West and East beaches, and hike to the Princess Cave (Phra Nang Cave) with its unique offerings and stunning lagoon viewpoint.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange a private rock climbing session on Railay's world-famous limestone karsts with a certified guide — suitable for beginners and experienced climbers alike. The dramatic views from the top are unforgettable. Alternatively, kayak through the mangrove lagoons and sea caves surrounding Railay.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the Railay Beach Club, followed by dinner at one of Railay's finest restaurants. Return to Phi Phi by private speedboat under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Continental breakfast at the hotel before departure — croissants, smoked salmon, fresh fruit, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at The Grotto Restaurant at Rayavadee Resort, Railay — an iconic cave restaurant serving premium Thai and international cuisine in a breathtaking setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Flame Restaurant, Railay — acclaimed for its live fire cooking, premium steaks, fresh seafood, and extensive cocktail menu

day_by_day.notes: Railay Beach is accessible only by longtail boat from Ao Nang or Krabi Town. The Phra Nang Cave lagoon hike is steep and can be muddy — wear appropriate footwear. Check weather and sea conditions before the return speedboat journey.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day premium excursion to James Bond Island (Khao Phing Kan) in Phang Nga Bay — depart from Krabi by private speedboat. Marvel at the iconic Tapu Island (the needle-like rock immortalized in The Man with the Golden Gun), explore the sea caves, and paddle through the limestone karsts by kayak.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the floating Muslim fishing village of Ko Panyi — a remarkable community built entirely on stilts over the water. Explore the village, visit the floating mosque, and browse local handicraft stalls. Kayak through the extraordinary Phang Nga Bay mangroves with a knowledgeable naturalist guide.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phi Phi by private speedboat. Enjoy a relaxed evening at your boutique stay — sundowner drinks on your private terrace, followed by a casual dinner at the hotel's beachfront restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel — Thai-style rice porridge, fried eggs, fresh fruit, and Thai iced tea
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at Ko Panyi floating village — famous for its fresh-caught fish, grilled squid, and crab curry served over the water
meals.dinner: Dinner at your boutique stay's restaurant — signature dishes of Andaman red curry, steamed sea bass with lime and chili, and coconut panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: This is a long day on the water — bring sun protection, a hat, and plenty of water. Phang Nga Bay is best explored at high tide for kayaking through the caves. Consider an overnight stay in Khao Lak or Phuket if the return journey is too long.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate a full morning to a private luxury yacht charter around the Phi Phi archipelago. Sail at your own pace, anchor at secluded bays inaccessible to larger boats, and enjoy complete privacy. The yacht comes with a professional crew, premium catering, and water sports equipment (paddleboards, snorkeling gear, and a sea scooter).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the yacht charter to a hidden snorkeling spot known only to local guides — pristine coral gardens with exceptional marine biodiversity. Enjoy afternoon tea and fresh fruit on deck as you cruise back toward Phi Phi with the golden afternoon light.
day_by_day.evening: Disembark and head to the Phi Phi Viewpoint for a final sunset view of the twin bays. Celebrate a week in paradise with a premium dinner at the island's finest restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast on the yacht deck — smoked salmon canapés, fresh pastries, tropical fruits, and sparkling wine
meals.lunch: Gourmet BBQ lunch prepared by the yacht chef — grilled lobster tails, tiger prawns, herb-marinated chicken, and fresh salads
meals.dinner: Dinner at Pee Pee Bakery & Restaurant — a hidden gem beloved by discerning travelers for its creative Thai-European fusion dishes and exceptional fresh seafood

day_by_day.notes: Private yacht charters require advance booking of at least 48–72 hours. Prices vary based on yacht size and duration. A half-day charter (4–5 hours) is a more affordable option without sacrificing the premium experience.

day_by_day.morning: Transfer by private speedboat to Phuket (approximately 1.5 hours). Check into a 5-star luxury resort in Surin Beach or Kamala Beach area. Spend the morning exploring Phuket's upscale Boat Lagoon Marina district and browsing the premium boutiques and art galleries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the iconic Big Buddha on Nakkerd Hill for panoramic views over Phuket. Explore the beautifully restored Sino-Portuguese architecture of Phuket Old Town — stroll along Thalang Road, Dibuk Road, and Soi Romanee, admiring the colorful shophouses and visiting artisan studios.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Phuket's legendary street food scene at the Phuket Sunday Walking Street (or Chillva Market if not a Sunday). Sample local Peranakan-influenced specialties including o-tao (oyster pancake), mee hun tom (noodle soup), and khanom jeen (rice noodles with curry).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel restaurant upon arrival — full international buffet with live cooking stations
meals.lunch: Lunch at Suay Restaurant, Phuket Town — award-winning contemporary Thai cuisine in a beautifully restored heritage shophouse
meals.dinner: Street food walking dinner at Phuket Old Town Night Market — guided tastings of 10+ authentic local specialties with a private food guide

day_by_day.notes: Phuket Old Town is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes. The Chillva Market operates Thursday through Sunday evenings. Book your 5-star Phuket resort in advance as October can still see good occupancy from European travelers.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning at Surin Beach or Kamala Beach — two of Phuket's most upscale and beautiful stretches of sand. Arrange a premium beach club experience at Catch Beach Club or HQ Beach Lounge — private sun beds, infinity pool access, and beachside service.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a private tuk-tuk tour to explore Phuket's hidden temples and local neighborhoods. Visit Wat Chalong — Phuket's most important Buddhist temple — and the Phuket Trickeye Museum for a fun cultural interlude. Stop at a premium Thai silk and handicraft boutique for souvenir shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner cruise around Phang Nga Bay or along Phuket's western coastline aboard a luxury catamaran. Enjoy premium canapés, cocktails, and a 3-course dinner as the sun melts into the Andaman Sea.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — tropical smoothie bar, eggs Benedict, and freshly baked Thai pastries
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café del Mar Phuket beach club — Mediterranean-inspired menu with fresh seafood, mezze platters, and signature cocktails
meals.dinner: Premium sunset dinner cruise — 3-course meal featuring tom kha goong, grilled Andaman lobster, and coconut ice cream, with complimentary Champagne

day_by_day.notes: Surin Beach is known as Phuket's 'Millionaire's Mile' and is popular with high-end travelers. Beach clubs here require reservations during peak periods. The sunset cruise departs from Chalong Pier — arrange private transfer from your hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Similan Islands — widely regarded as one of the top 10 diving and snorkeling destinations in the world. Depart from Phuket by private speedboat (approximately 1.5 hours). Snorkel or dive among massive granite boulders, swim-throughs, and extraordinary marine life including whale sharks (seasonal), manta rays, and sea turtles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore multiple Similan Islands — hike to Donald Duck Bay viewpoint on Island 8 for dramatic panoramic views, relax on the impossibly white beach of Island 4, and snorkel the vibrant reef at Island 9. Your private guide will curate the best spots based on current conditions.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phuket by speedboat in the late afternoon. Enjoy a final luxurious evening — treat yourself to a premium Thai spa experience at your resort's wellness center, followed by a farewell dinner at one of Phuket's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel before departure — fruit, yogurt, granola, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch on a Similan Island beach — grilled whole fish, green papaya salad, sticky rice, and fresh coconuts
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Acqua Restaurant, Phuket — one of Phuket's most acclaimed fine dining establishments, offering an exquisite Italian-Mediterranean tasting menu with panoramic sea views

day_by_day.notes: The Similan Islands are a National Marine Park — entrance fees apply. The islands are typically only open October through May, making this an ideal time to visit. Confirm current operating status before booking. This is a long day — depart by 7:00 AM for maximum time on the islands.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Thailand — enjoy a leisurely breakfast at your resort. Take one last dip in the pool or a quiet walk on the beach to soak in the Andaman atmosphere. Visit a premium Thai spa for a final 60-minute traditional Thai massage to prepare your body for the long flight home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute luxury shopping at Jungceylon Mall in Patong or Central Festival Phuket — pick up premium Thai silk, artisan ceramics, high-quality massage oils, and gourmet Thai food products as souvenirs. Arrange a private transfer to Phuket International Airport with ample time before your departure flight.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Phuket International Airport. Enjoy the airport's premium lounges and reflect on an extraordinary 13-day journey through Thailand's most spectacular islands, beaches, and culinary landscapes.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast buffet at the hotel — every Thai and international favorite one last time, with fresh-pressed juices and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Premium lunch at the airport or a final street food stop near the hotel — a last bowl of authentic pad thai or khao pad from a beloved local spot
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight premium meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your international flight for check-in and security at Phuket Airport. Pre-book your airport transfer the evening before. Consider purchasing travel insurance that covers flight delays. Ensure all souvenirs comply with Thai export regulations — Buddha images and antiques may require permits.

query: Thailand beaches, $1800 for couple, mix of island hopping and street food, October 2026
